ds: Fraudsters pose as banks, police, tax authorities or delivery firms by phone, SMS or email, harvesting credentials or inducing customers to move money. The criminal often spoofs numbers and uses urgency and fear.

src.t: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)
FCA, consumer warnings on impersonation fraud (general)
FinCEN (US Treasury), FinCEN Alert on Money Laundering Activity Associated with Digital Asset Investment Scam Centers (FIN-2026-Alert005) (2026-09-03)

cn.rt: Victims called or texted by impersonators and induced to share codes or move money; card details loaded to wallets.

rat: Victims contacted by phone, SMS or email and induced to share codes or move money; card details used at new merchants and wallets.

ind.n: Customer reports unsolicited call or text from 'the bank'
ind.cx: Victim-side: contact claims to be from the bank's fraud team and requests action, codes or transfers.
ind.ds: contact claims to be from the bank's fraud team and requests action, codes or transfers.

ind.n: One-time passcode shared or requested during a call
ind.cx: Victim-side: authentication codes are read out or entered while the customer is on a live call.
ind.ds: authentication codes are read out or entered while the customer is on a live call.

ind.n: Login from new device shortly after phishing click
ind.cx: Attacker-side: credentials harvested via a fake site are used on an unfamiliar device or location.
ind.ds: Session originates from a device, country, emulator or network not previously associated with the customer, including shortly after a phishing event.
ind.cn: Login from unfamiliar device, location or infrastructure

ind.n: Spoofed phone number matching the bank's real number
ind.cx: Outbound spoofing makes calls appear genuine; call-detail records reveal the discrepancy.
ind.ds: Outbound spoofing makes calls appear genuine; call-detail records reveal the discrepancy.

ind.n: Mass of near-identical SMS or links referencing parcels or fines
ind.cx: Bank brand impersonation campaigns observed in threat feeds and customer reports.
ind.ds: Bank brand impersonation campaigns observed in threat feeds and customer reports.

ind.n: Customer instructed to move money to a 'safe' account
ind.cx: Victim-side: pretext of protection leads to transfers to unfamiliar accounts.
ind.ds: Victim-side: pretext of protection leads to transfers to unfamiliar accounts.

ind.n: Mule accounts receiving phished funds then cashing out
ind.cx: Receiving accounts withdraw cash or buy crypto promptly after credits.
ind.ds: A new or low-activity account receives payments from several unrelated individuals who appear to be victims of fraud or phishing, followed by onward movement or cash-out.
ind.cn: Account receiving funds from multiple apparent fraud victims

ind.n: Payment card details used at new merchants immediately after a call
ind.cx: Victim-side: card details given verbally are used for online purchases or wallet provisioning.
ind.ds: Victim-side: card details given verbally are used for online purchases or wallet provisioning.

ind.n: Spike in digital wallet provisioning on one customer card
ind.cx: Attacker provisions the card to multiple wallets after obtaining one-time codes.
ind.ds: Attacker provisions the card to multiple wallets after obtaining one-time codes.

ind.n: Customer says an official told them to pay in crypto, gold, gift cards or by international wire
ind.cx: Government or police impersonation: the 'official' directs payment in crypto, gift cards, precious metals or by international wire.
ind.fp: Genuine tax or fine payments made through official, verifiable channels.
ind.ds: The customer explains a payment as instructed by someone claiming to be police, a regulator or another government body, using digital assets, precious metals, gift cards or an overseas wire.

ind.n: Savings or retirement funds withdrawn to buy gold that is handed to a courier
ind.cx: Victim told to convert savings to gold and hand it to a courier for 'safekeeping'.
ind.fp: Genuine bullion investment held in the customer's own custody or a recognised vault.
ind.ds: The customer liquidates investment or retirement savings to buy bullion or gold and says they have been told to hand it to a courier or collector.

ctl.ds: Provides targeted messaging that helps customers recognise scam scripts and mule recruitment, verify requests independently and use trusted routes for giving or paying. It reduces victimisation and unwitting participation.
Verifies instructions, detail changes and unusual requests by contacting the customer on a channel held on file, never one supplied in the request. It defeats impersonation and account takeover.
Monitors for spoofed domains, fake apps, adverts, numbers and fraudulent campaigns, and arranges takedown, suspension and customer alerts. It removes criminal infrastructure.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

ctl.n: Dynamic payment friction and scam warnings
ctl.ds: Risk-scored payments trigger a purpose question and a tailored scam warning, or a call-back, before release to the customer. It gives the customer a chance to reconsider and interrupts payments made under deception.
Requires phishing-resistant authentication and additional verification on risky sessions, credential or payee changes and large payments. It blocks unauthorised access and payments.

Fingerprints devices, IP addresses, emulators and network attributes to link applications, sessions and accounts and to flag shared or anomalous infrastructure. It exposes mule rings and multiple-account abuse.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

Checks the payee name against the destination account before release and warns on no-match or close-match, and flags payee-name mismatches against contracted entities. It interrupts misdirected, spoofed and fraudulent payments.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

Authenticates the cardholder at online checkout through an additional challenge and replaces stored card numbers with tokens. It blocks use of stolen card details and shifts liability for unauthorised transactions.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

Allows customers to nominate a trusted contact and applies tailored handling and permitted escalation when vulnerability is flagged. It adds a safeguard for customers more exposed to manipulation or coercion.
